rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a poor-quality early/low-grade blastocyst and absent/degenerate ICM/TE, but it adds uncertain image-specific details and some hedging about stage that are not firmly supported from a single still.

Integrates age, BMI, endometriosis, endometrial thickness, ovarian response, sperm parameters, and first-cycle status with embryo quality reasonably well, though AMH is unavailable and some interactions are only briefly developed.

Overall logic is clear: very poor embryo morphology is the dominant negative factor, partially offset by favorable uterine and general health factors. Minor inconsistencies remain around exact stage interpretation and prognosis framing.

Largely aligned with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF counseling, including cautious single-embryo transfer framing, no bed rest, and selective rather than routine PGT-A. Some speculative comments are less guideline-based.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer, counseling, luteal support, follow-up, and future cycle review including ovarian reserve reassessment and endometriosis-focused planning, though some recommendations remain somewhat general.
